newsitem.title: FRANCE: French insurer AGF denies takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: French insurer AGF denies takeover talk.

text.p: French insurer AGF denied on Tuesday market talk it would bid for rivals GAN or Athena and sought to knock down rumours German insurer Allianz might make it a takeover target.
"The rumours we're going to acquire either GAN or Athena (100 percent owned by Worms & Cie) are totally unfounded," an AGF spokesman said.
"It's also not in Allianz's tradition to go into costly, unfriendly takeovers," he said. "We don't think it's in the works." Allianz could not be reached for comment.

The bid talk swept shares of both recently privatised AGF and government-controlled GAN higher on Tuesday. AGF rose 5.00 percent to 189.0 francs and GAN jumped 6.76 percent to 112.1 francs. Worms fell 0.55 percent to 361.0 francs.

The buying was triggered by an article in the business daily La Tribune about AGF's future in light of the multi-billion dollar takeover by French insurer Axa of competitor UAP late last year, creating the world's second-biggest insurer.
The article said growing concentration in the sector meant Assurances Generales de France (AGF) needed to move fast to protect its independence and develop critical mass.
After the surprise Axa-UAP linkup, insurance analysts said they were unwilling to rule out any scenario. "Once bitten, twice shy," said one.
Talk that Allianz could be interested in moving into AGF's capital or in bidding for loss-making insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) when it is privatised has been simmering for some time.

Last month, Allianz's payment of 2.25 billion francs for Navigation Mixte's 34 percent stake in its Allianz Via unit was seen by some analysts as a desire to respond decisively to the consolidation in the French market.
Analysts said whether AGF launched a bid for GAN would depend on how the government privatised the insurer.
"Everything has a price," said one analyst. "If the insurance operations were stripped out and the property exposure removed, it could be an interesting operation."
Analysts added that AGF would not be too costly for Allianz. "Certainly AGF is not expensive, Allianz could afford it," said one.
"But it's not an aggressive company in terms of making hostile bids. If it has ambitions, I think it is more with (French state-owned bank) Credit Lyonnais," he said.
Allianz has long been mentioned as interested in buying into Credit Lyonnais when it is privatised. Credit Lyonnais already sells Allianz products over its counters.

The analyst said reports that Allianz plans to put Dominique Bazy, recruited from the merged Axa-UAP group and former number three at Credit Lyonnais, in charge of its French operations, favoured such a scenario.
Another analyst said Allianz Via had not been "its greatest buy" and that at analysts' meetings it has talked more about its desire to get into the Pacific Rim and build its British operations.
